sources.citation: Ollett, Andrew. 2017. Language of the Snakes: Prakrit, Sanskrit, and the Language Order of Premodern India. Oakland: University of California Press (Luminos OA).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Paisaci appears only as a grammarians' category (pp. 135, 152-153, 162 and notes). pp. 89-90 on Prakrit generally: leaves open whether Prakrit kept the Vedic mobile accent (Pischel) or had Latin-like rules fixing accent two or three syllables from the end (Jacobi); nothing Paisaci-specific.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3247.42; a Harvard library, call number Bc 0260
sources.note: Paisaci section: segmental features and the home-of-Paisaci debate only. The book's sole accent note (sec. 67 note, p. 26) concerns Maharastri (Vedic) vs Sauraseni (classical Skt), not Paisaci.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1912. Paisaci, Pisacas, and 'Modern Pisaca'. ZDMG 66: 49-86.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: sec. 1 'What was Paisaci Prakrit?' (pp. 49-60) tabulates every rule of Vararuci ch. 10, Hemacandra IV.303-328 and Kumarapalacarita VIII.6-13: consonant treatment and morphology only; no accent/stress statement anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Konow, Sten. 1910. The home of Paisaci. ZDMG 64: 95-118.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Compares grammarians' Paisaci phonology with Magadhi and NW dialects (p. 105 ff.); no accent/stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent the article range for accent/stress/Betonung: only 'lays stress on' idiom).

sources.citation: Pischel, Richard. 1900. Grammatik der Prakrit-Sprachen (Grundriss der indo-arischen Philologie I.8). Strassburg: Truebner. sec. 27 (pp. 27-31) Paisaci; sec. 46 (p. 48) Accent.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: sec. 46: 'Der Accent von M. AMg. JM., dem poetischen A., voraussichtlich auch JS., entspricht wesentlich dem vedischen.. In S. Mg. Dh. ist auch der Accent des classischen Skt. nachweisbar' -- Paisaci (P., CP.) is not named. sec. 27 on Paisaci gives only segmental features (devoicing, non-elision, n>n, l>l) and reports the folk belief that bhutas speak 'mit einem naeselnden Accent', adding 'Die Grammatiker erwaehnen davon nichts'. No Paisaci word-accent statement.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1906. The Pisaca Languages of North-Western India (Asiatic Society Monographs 8). London: Royal Asiatic Society. pp. 8-12 'Paisaci and Culika-Paisacika'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Digest of Hemacandra IV.303-328 (phonetics + accidence): all segmental, no accent statement. The word 'accent' occurs only in the transcription note for the modern Dardic languages (p. 14: 'An acute accent indicates the stress-syllable'). Book actually describes Dardic ('Modern Pisaca'), not Paisaci Prakrit.

sources.citation: Pischel, Richard (1900). Grammatik der Prakrit-Sprachen. Strassburg: Trübner. 429 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KG 13151; a Harvard library, call number Bc 0220)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number KG 13151; a Harvard library, call number Bc 0220
sources.note: Catalog has no record for pais1238. § 46 is about other Prakrits (not-about-this-language for the accent claim); for Paisaci specifically the work is silent. Since Hc. IV.323 (cited by Pischel) makes Paisaci follow Sauraseni in everything not specially ruled, one could infer the Sauraseni (classical-Skt/Latin-type) accent for Paisaci, but Pischel does not draw that inference and it is not recorded here as a reading.
